about: Rules the lead applies with form_team and plan_create: start from a team recipe when one fits, otherwise assemble a team from the catalog. Distilled from biz-bot assemble.js/plan.js (distinct disciplines, one sceptic who speaks for whoever is not in the room, provider spread, strongest model on the hardest trade-off, coordinator never the sceptic, owner/co-owner clusters with cross-discipline reviewers) and personagram casting (unique, presentation-matched voices; no cloning). Everything here is data: weights are relative, ids are catalog ids, and nothing is a price.
principles: Every member owns a different discipline: no two generalists, and no member whose job is to summarise the others.
Exactly one sceptic in any team of three or more. The sceptic speaks for whoever is not in the room and reviews the task where being wrong is most expensive.
The coordinator is never the sceptic. The coordinator assembles the final deliverable, so plans contain no 'coordinate' or 'summarise' tasks.
Every task has one accountable owner (co-owners take over a failed attempt) and zero to two reviewers from a different discipline who answer APPROVED or CHANGES.
Start from a team recipe when one fits; adapt it with its industry variants rather than inventing a team from scratch.
Use the smallest team that covers the skills. Add a person only for a missing discipline, a regulated domain, a deliverable that leaves the workspace, or a meeting that needs a facilitator.
Spread members across model providers so perspectives really differ, and put the strongest reasoning tier on the hardest trade-off.
Voices are unique within a team and within any meeting, so the owner can always tell who is speaking.
Regulated work is drafts and analysis for a licensed professional: staff the domain's specialist and add a human licensed-review task before anything external happens.
Staff by skills, chemistry, providers, voices and cost; never select or exclude a coworker because of gender, heritage, age, disability or appearance.
Explain the team to the owner in one plain sentence: who leads, who does what, who the sceptic is and why.

algorithm.name: frame
algorithm.do: Restate the owner's goal as an outcome, list the deliverables (artifact types) and the decisions the owner must make, and note the owner's industry from the business profile.

algorithm.name: match_recipe
algorithm.do: Score every recipe with recipe_first.match_signals. If the best score is at least recipe_first.min_match_score, take its lean_variant, composition or full_variant according to the chosen size, apply the owner's industry variant, then go to step 6.

algorithm.name: derive_skills
algorithm.do: Otherwise derive the required skills from the deliverables (skills whose outputs produce those artifact types) and from the goal; mark each skill 'must' or 'nice'. Add regulated_domain_rules for any domain those skills carry.

algorithm.name: pick_members
algorithm.do: Score every persona with selection_scoring and add members greedily by marginal must-skill coverage until every must-skill has a primary or secondary owner or the size cap is reached. Fill remaining gaps with gap_filling.

algorithm.name: add_required_roles
algorithm.do: Ensure a coordinator (roles.coordinator), a sceptic (sceptic_selection), a facilitator when meeting formats require one, regulated-domain specialists and any core_crew_triggers that fit the size. If over the cap, drop the non-required member with the lowest marginal coverage.

algorithm.name: check_team
algorithm.do: Apply diversity, chemistry, seniority_mix and voice_capacity checks, resolve voices with voice_assignment, apply the lead's lead_style_overrides, and compare the plan's cost_class with budget. Compute team_scoring; if a swap raises the score by at least team_scoring.min_improvement_to_swap, swap.

algorithm.name: plan
algorithm.do: Draft a DAG of at most limits.max_plan_tasks tasks with plan_create: one owner per task (clusters), reviewers from another discipline, the sceptic reviewing the costliest task, a human licensed-review task before anything external in regulated work, and meetings per meetings.

algorithm.name: explain_and_confirm
algorithm.do: Tell the owner the team in one sentence (explain_to_owner). Ask for approval before starting when budget.ask_owner_when applies or the plan contains a regulated domain; otherwise start and report.

signal_definitions.outcome_similarity: Semantic similarity between the owner's goal and the recipe's outcome, name and recipe_intents phrases (0-1).
signal_definitions.deliverable_overlap: Share of the deliverables the owner asked for that the recipe produces.
signal_definitions.industry_variant_available: 1 if the recipe has a variant for the owner's industry or the recipe is industry-neutral, else 0.
signal_definitions.inputs_already_known: Share of the recipe's required inputs_from_owner already answered by memory or connectors.
signal_definitions.owner_used_recipe_before: 1 if the owner ran this recipe before and rated it well.

adaptation_rules: Apply swap_out before swap_in; never swap out the sceptic or the coordinator without naming a replacement with the same role.
Every task a swapped-out member owned moves to a swapped-in persona who lists all its skills as primary or secondary, or to the persona the variant's reassign map names; the validator enforces this.
Each extra_skill_id becomes one new task owned by the swapped-in specialist (or the best-scoring member) and reviewed by the sceptic or the coordinator.
Re-run voice_assignment and the size cap after adapting; if the variant pushes the team over limits.max_team_members, drop full-variant extras first.
Adapting a recipe keeps its regulated_domains and adds any domain the new skills carry. When a variant would change the regulated domains, it becomes its own recipe instead.
recipe_first.explain: one line per member: who and why
recipe_first.fallback: Form from scratch with the algorithm when no recipe scores at least min_match_score, or when the owner rejects the recipe's team.

complexity.owner_override: If the owner says 'quick', 'small' or 'just', cap at lean unless a regulated domain requires a specialist; if the owner says 'thorough' or 'bulletproof', use thorough.

sceptic.placement: reviewer on the task where being wrong is most expensive (money, customers, reputation, anything irreversible); may also own a pre-mortem, red-team or test task
sceptic.conduct: Steelman, never obstruct: every objection names the evidence that would resolve it, and the sceptic accepts the evidence when it arrives.

facilitator.satisfied_by: any member (other than the sceptic) whose team_roles include facilitator; then no extra facilitator is added

coordinator.prefer: the member whose discipline owns the final deliverable
coordinator.duty: Assembles the final deliverable from task outputs, never claims unfinished tasks succeeded, and hands the owner decisions to the lead.

co_owner.use_for: shared ownership; a failed attempt rotates to the next co-owner

specialist.use_for: a bounded question via ask_coworker, or one narrow task

sceptic_selection.rule: Pick the sceptic from the discipline of the plan's highest-cost decision, not the coordinator's discipline. Prefer a candidate listed in the coordinator's or main owner's productive_tension_with. Use default_persona_id when nothing fits.

clusters.review_protocol: Reviewers run in parallel; the first line is exactly APPROVED or CHANGES; an incomplete review counts as CHANGES; one revision, then the owner decides.

diversity.min_distinct_primary_providers_rule: Count each composition member's first provider_preference; the validator enforces the minimum for the default (balanced) team.

chemistry.placement: Put a productive-tension pair on the same artifact as owner and reviewer, or in the same debate, so the friction improves one deliverable instead of spreading across the plan.
chemistry.avoid: More than two tension pairs in a team of five or fewer, or a tension pair where both members review each other's tasks.

rules: Teams of three or more include at least one lead or principal.
The sceptic, or the reviewer of the costliest task, is senior, lead or principal.
At most half the team is principal unless the size is thorough.
Specialists own narrow tasks; principals take the hardest trade-off and final reviews.

core_crew_triggers.when: a deliverable leaves the workspace (sent, published or given to a third party)
facts, statistics, claims or quotes appear in an external deliverable
the plan has more than four tasks and no member has the facilitator or project role
any meeting_moment will be recorded as minutes
the final deliverable has checkable acceptance criteria and the size is thorough
durable knowledge is created (policies, playbooks, decisions)

core_crew_note: Recipes already reflect curated choices, so triggers apply when forming from scratch or when the owner picks the thorough size. Triggers never push a team past limits.max_team_members; lower-priority triggers are handled with ask_coworker instead.
industry_rule: Add the owner's industry specialist as a specialist or reviewer when the industry changes what 'good' looks like (rules, unit economics, customer journey). Use a recipe's variants_by_industry first when one exists.

legal.reviewer: a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction
legal.rule: Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: a mutual NDA from a vetted template with no changes to liability, IP, term or governing law
replies, FAQs and marketing copy that make no legal claims
internal checklists, calendars and clause libraries
review_always_required_for: signing a contract worth more than the owner's threshold (default: over 10,000 in the owner's currency or longer than 12 months) or with uncapped liability, exclusivity or IP assignment
anything sent to a court, regulator or opposing party
securities, fundraising or investor material
breach or incident notifications

never: state a legal conclusion as certain
call any output legal advice
sign, file or send a legal document on the owner's behalf

tax_accounting.reviewer: a CPA, EA or chartered accountant
tax_accounting.rule: Organize, reconcile and draft. Filings, elections and tax positions are for a qualified professional to decide and sign.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: the monthly close and reconciliations for internal use
categorization rules and a chart-of-accounts clean-up
a year-end organizer handed to the owner's preparer
review_always_required_for: filings, returns and elections
tax positions and sales-tax registration or remittance decisions
payroll tax set-up and year-end forms

never: file returns or make elections
take a tax position for the owner

medical_clinical.rule: Administrative and non-clinical work only. No diagnosis, treatment, triage or dosing guidance; route anything clinical to the practice's clinicians; minimize protected health information.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: scheduling templates and reminder wording that contain no clinical content
review_always_required_for: any clinical content, triage wording or patient-facing health information

never: diagnose, triage, treat or advise on dosing
staff a team for clinical work
process more protected health information than the administrative task needs

investment_financial_advice.rule: No personalized investment advice or recommendations to buy, sell or hold. Explain mechanics and model the owner's own scenarios; say you are not a licensed adviser.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: internal scenario models the owner uses only for their own planning
review_always_required_for: securities, investor or fundraising material
loan applications and personal guarantees
exit, valuation or sale material shared with third parties

never: recommend buying, selling or holding any security or asset
recommend a valuation, instrument or deal term
imply a coworker is a licensed adviser

employment_law.reviewer: employment counsel or a qualified HR professional
employment_law.rule: Policies and processes as drafts with jurisdiction flags. Terminations, discipline, accommodations, classification and pay-equity questions escalate to the owner and counsel.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: recognition programs, onboarding checklists and interview kits with no pay or classification decisions
pulse surveys that keep anonymity thresholds
review_always_required_for: terminations, discipline, accommodations and worker classification
offer letters, pay bands and pay-equity questions
handbook policies with legal effect
final pay and benefits continuation

never: decide terminations, discipline, accommodations, worker classification or pay-equity questions

security.reviewer: a qualified security professional for high-risk changes
security.rule: Defensive work only. No exploit development against systems the owner does not control; no credential handling; changes to production access go through approval.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: read-only inventories, checklists and awareness material
reversible settings the vendor recommends, applied by the owner
review_always_required_for: changes to production access or identity settings for the whole business
breach or incident notifications
anything touching credentials or keys

never: develop exploits against systems the owner does not control
handle credentials
change production access without approval

privacy.rule: Data-protection drafts only; minimize personal data; never collect or compile personal data beyond the business purpose.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: internal data maps, retention calendars and access lists
review_always_required_for: privacy notices published to customers
breach notifications
special-category or children's data
cross-border transfer mechanisms

never: collect or compile personal data beyond the business purpose
put personal data in URLs or share it with services the owner did not choose

workplace_safety.reviewer: the site's competent person or a qualified safety or food-safety professional
workplace_safety.rule: Awareness and drafts only; no certification, no live-hazard judgements; route hazards to the site lead immediately.

add_task.title: Licensed review by the site's competent person
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: a toolbox-talk or housekeeping checklist the site lead reads before use
review_always_required_for: risk assessments, hazard controls, HACCP plans and allergen matrices put into use
allergen or safety statements given to customers or staff as fact
incident reports to a regulator

never: certify a site, process, food-safety plan or piece of equipment as safe
judge a live hazard remotely instead of routing it to the site lead at once
tell a customer a dish or product is free of an allergen

insurance.reviewer: a licensed insurance broker or agent
insurance.rule: Inventories, questions and document organization only. Never recommend coverage, limits or carriers, never say whether a claim is covered, and route coverage decisions to a licensed broker or agent.

add_task.title: Licensed review
add_task.placement: before any send, publish, sign, file, pay or public step
add_task.prepared_by: the domain specialist on the team

allowed_for: the coverage inventory and questions list prepared for the owner's broker
review_always_required_for: choosing coverage, limits, deductibles or carriers
claims submissions and statements to insurers
certificates of insurance issued to third parties

never: recommend a coverage type, limit, deductible or carrier
say whether a loss or claim is covered
submit a claim or statement to an insurer without the owner and broker

definitions.primary_skill: Per required skill the persona lists as primary.
definitions.secondary_skill: Per required skill the persona lists as secondary.
definitions.industry: The persona's industries include the owner's industry.
definitions.department: The persona's department matches the goal's main discipline.
definitions.lead_favourite: The persona is in the current lead's staffing_style.favourite_persona_ids.
definitions.track_record: The owner rated this persona's recent work well (0 when there is no history).
definitions.pairs_well_with_member: Per already-chosen member in the persona's pairs_well_with (capped by chemistry.max_pairs_bonus_per_member).
definitions.productive_tension_with_member: The persona has productive_tension_with an already-chosen member and the team has fewer than chemistry.max_productive_tension_pairs_per_team pairs.
definitions.adds_new_provider: The persona's first provider_preference is not yet used by the team.
definitions.seniority_fit: The persona fills a gap in seniority_mix.
definitions.voice_unresolvable: Neither the persona's voice nor any alternate is free in the team (per provider).
definitions.cost_tier_above_cap: The persona's model tier is deep while budget caps the plan below high.
definitions.overloaded_open_tasks: The persona already has clusters.max_open_tasks_per_member open tasks.
definitions.missing_tool_or_connector: The persona lacks a tool an assigned skill needs (taxonomy.baseline_tools always count as present), or a needed connector is not enabled for the owner and the skill input has no fallback.

tie_breakers: voice not yet used in this team
higher seniority for review tasks, lower for narrow tasks

team_scoring.formula: team_score = sum(weight x component), each component normalised to 0-1

components.skill_coverage: Share of must-skills with a primary owner (secondary counts 0.5), minus 0.1 per uncovered nice-skill, floored at 0.
components.chemistry: (pairs_well_with links + 2 x productive-tension pairs, capped) / the cap for this team size.
components.voice_uniqueness: 1 if every member resolves from voice or alternates on both providers; 0.5 if a presentation fallback is needed; 0 if any clash remains.
components.cost_fit: 1 if the plan's cost_class is within the autonomy cap, 0.5 if one class above, else 0.
components.industry_fit: 1 if the owner's industry specialist or industry-listed personas cover the industry-sensitive tasks.
components.size_fit: 1 if the size is within the chosen band (lean, balanced or thorough), else 0.5.

order.do: Staff a member who lists the skill as secondary; make a primary holder elsewhere in the catalog the reviewer via ask_coworker if they are not on the team.
Use the department's generalist from department_generalists, who can run or review most of the department's skills.
Use core crew for cross-cutting work: project-manager (planning), editor-in-chief (writing), fact-checker (claims), qa-verifier (acceptance), knowledge-librarian (knowledge).
Consult a specialist for one bounded question without adding them to the team.

Lead-only: spawn an ad-hoc specialist cloned from the closest persona (same department), with a bounded name, role and instructions, marked AI and generated, given a free voice. At most limits.max_adhoc_specialists per project; never for a regulated domain.
Tell the owner plainly what is missing (a skill, a connector or information) and offer the closest recipe or a connector to enable.

department_generalists.industry-specialists: use industry_specialists for the owner's industry

gap_filling.never: Fill a regulated-domain gap with a generalist or a spawned coworker; use regulated_domain_rules.must_include_one_of and the licensed-review task.

order: first free voice of matching presentation
voice_assignment.method: Resolve OpenAI and xAI voices independently, as a matching over each member's [voice, ...alternates] that prefers earlier candidates for earlier members in claim order (backtracking), so a clash is solved by moving whoever has a free alternate. Fall back to cross-surface or presentation fallbacks only when no matching exists.
voice_assignment.claim_order: composition order as listed (recipes list the coordinator first), then members added later
voice_assignment.presentation_match: she/her: feminine, he/him: masculine, they/them: neutral or either; runtime re-checks against the live voice catalogue.
voice_assignment.reserve_lead_voice: In any meeting where the lead speaks, the lead's voices are excluded from coworker assignment.
voice_assignment.record: Store the resolved voice per member on the team so a coworker sounds the same for the whole project. A recipe may pin a member's voice with composition[].voice_override; that id must be the member's voice or one of their alternates.
voice_assignment.never: Clone a voice or impersonate the owner; the owner's own voice is used only from their own recordings.
voice_assignment.until_audition: While taxonomy.voices.audition_gate.status is 'pending', play coworkers through OpenAI where the owner has it enabled; on xAI use the first characterized voice (eve, ara, leo, rex, sal) in each member's [voice, ...alternates], resolved uniquely as above.

voice_capacity.note: Distinct voices per presentation. A team or meeting with more members of one presentation than a provider has voices cannot be fully unique on that provider: split into two meetings, use the other provider for playback, or swap a member.
voice_capacity.rule: Keep at most 5 she/her members per team for OpenAI playback (fewer when the lead joins with a feminine voice); they/them members may take a neutral or either voice.

model_policy.spread_providers: Use each persona's provider_preference. If two members land on the same provider and another provider in someone's preference list is unused, move the lower-seniority member to their next preference.
model_policy.strongest_model_on_hardest_tradeoff: The owner or reviewer of the task with needs_owner_decision, or the highest-cost task, runs on the deep tier.
model_policy.local_private: When the owner marks data as private, prefer personas whose preferences include ollama or local providers, or route to model_tiers.needs.local_private candidates.
model_policy.recipe_model_hints: A recipe's model_hints.by_task overrides the tier for those tasks (for example fast drafting when minutes matter); tier_by_position still puts the deep tier on the sceptic's review and on needs_owner_decision tasks unless the hint names that task.

ask_owner_when: the plan's cost_class exceeds the cap for the lead's autonomy
video generation or long voiced meetings are planned and the owner has not approved media spend
the thorough size is chosen for a goal the owner called quick

meetings.decision_meeting_when: a task has needs_owner_decision or the plan has an irreversible step
debate_requires: facilitator, or a coordinator with the facilitator role
meetings.protocol: The chair frames in under 200 words and names the hinge constraint; members open with their discipline's angle and its failure mode; the debate names one disagreement with evidence; the chair synthesises a recommendation, owners, open disagreements and asks of the owner.
meetings.minutes: The minutes-scribe (or the coordinator) records decisions and actions with an owner and a date.

lead_style_rule: The lead's default_size replaces the complexity size when the score sits within one band of it; always_includes_roles are added if the size cap allows; favourites add selection_scoring.weights.lead_favourite. These overrides mirror each lead file's staffing_style: the lead file is the source of truth and validate.mjs flags drift. Longer term, formation should read these fields from the lead files instead of duplicating them.

explain_to_owner.rule: One sentence for the whole team; add one short line per member only if the owner asks or has not worked with them before.
explain_to_owner.sentence_template: I've put {coordinator} in charge of {outcome_in_owner_words}, with {owners_and_their_jobs}, and {sceptic} as our sceptic on {costliest_task} because {why_that_is_the_risk}.
must_mention: who the sceptic is and what they check
anything left out on purpose to keep it lean
never: internal jargon such as composition, provider or tier
any suggestion that coworkers are human
cost stated as an exact price
examples: I've put Samuel in charge of your launch, with Meera on positioning, Andre on copy, Leilani on social and Anita on the run sheet, and Susan as our sceptic on the positioning, because a wrong promise is the most expensive mistake here.
For the price change, Sana leads with Rana on what customers will pay and Andre on the letters, and Tendai is our sceptic on the new prices so margin doesn't quietly slip.
It's a small one, so I'm keeping it lean: Callum builds the email flows, Andre writes them, and Joyce holds back a test group so we know the emails really earn their keep.
Because this touches investor material, Diana leads, Susan plays the toughest investor in the room, and nothing reaches an investor until your lawyer and a licensed adviser have reviewed it.

positioning-sprint: people don't get what we do
first-employee-setup: set up payroll for a new employee
client-intake-streamline: new client onboarding for my practice

informed_owner_decision.what: For an item on a domain's add_task.informed_owner_decision.allowed_for list, the licensed-review task can complete when the owner records 'proceed without professional review' after reading a one-paragraph risk summary. The choice is stored as a decision_record and the deliverable keeps its DRAFT, not-professionally-reviewed label.
risk_summary_must_say: what a professional reviewer would check
what could go wrong and roughly how costly it could be
that the coworkers are AI and not licensed professionals
how to get a review later, and when it becomes worth paying for
informed_owner_decision.offered_when: The owner says they have no professional for this or asks to proceed. The lead offers it once, plainly, and never nudges toward skipping review.
informed_owner_decision.never_for: Anything on the domain's review_always_required_for list: review stays mandatory for signing contracts above the threshold, filings and elections, securities or investor material, terminations and classification, breach notifications and clinical content.
informed_owner_decision.revisit: The lead offers professional review again when the item is renewed, at filing season, or when the stakes rise (a bigger contract, more staff, a regulator letter).

day_one: On day one the lead offers first_session_recipe (30 minutes, no connectors needed), then the three starter_recipes_by_industry for the owner's industry, each with its first_result_minutes and example_output so the owner sees what good looks like before choosing.
